title: What Happens If You Don't Sleep for 11 Days? (The 264-Hour Experiment)

scenes.narration_text: In December nineteen sixty-three, two high school kids in San Diego flipped a coin.

visual.description: SCENE_001: Hero (idle_neutral, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: They were not deciding who would take out the trash.

visual.description: SCENE_002: Hero (thinking, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: They were deciding who would stop sleeping for eleven straight days.

visual.description: SCENE_003: Hero (shocked_fall, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Their names were Randy Gardner and Bruce McAllister.

visual.description: SCENE_004: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: They wanted to win first prize at the Greater San Diego Science Fair.

visual.description: SCENE_005: Hero (celebrate_win, happy) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: And their plan was terrifyingly simple.

visual.description: SCENE_006: Hero (thinking, eager) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Beat the world record of two hundred and sixty hours without sleep.

visual.description: SCENE_007: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: No coffee. No caffeine pills.

visual.description: SCENE_008: Hero (idle_neutral, flat) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: No stimulant drugs of any kind.

visual.description: SCENE_009: Hero (thinking, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Just a teenager, two friends with a notebook, and a ticking clock.

visual.description: SCENE_010: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in office.
SCENE_011: Hero (idle_neutral, neutral) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Most of us feel like a walking zombie after pulling just one all-nighter.

visual.description: SCENE_012: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Your eyes burn, your head throbs, and you reread the same sentence four times.

visual.description: SCENE_013: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: So what actually happens inside your body when you stay awake for eleven days?

visual.description: SCENE_014: Hero (thinking, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Let us walk through the experiment hour by hour.

visual.description: SCENE_015: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: And see why Guinness World Records eventually banned anyone from trying this again.

visual.description: SCENE_016: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_017: Hero (idle_neutral, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: At the twenty-four-hour mark, Randy actually felt surprisingly fine.

visual.description: SCENE_018: Hero (celebrate_win, happy) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: If you have ever stayed up all night, you know that strange second wind.

visual.description: SCENE_019: Hero (idea_lightbulb, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: That is not real energy. That is your brain panicking.

visual.description: SCENE_020: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: When you miss a full night of sleep, your nervous system assumes danger.

visual.description: SCENE_021: Hero (running_hurry, eager) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: It floods your bloodstream with cortisol and adrenaline to keep your eyes open.

visual.description: SCENE_022: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: For a few hours, you feel wired, talkative, and almost euphoric.

visual.description: SCENE_023: Hero (celebrate_win, happy) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Researchers call this the dopamine rebound phase.

visual.description: SCENE_024: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Your brain boosts dopamine in a desperate attempt to keep your cortex running.

visual.description: SCENE_025: Hero (thinking, eager) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_026: Hero (stressed_headache, flat) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: By hour thirty-six, that chemical illusion collapses.

visual.description: SCENE_027: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: On day two, a chemical called adenosine has piled up like uncollected garbage.

visual.description: SCENE_028: Hero (pointing_target, flat) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Every waking hour, your neurons burn energy and leave adenosine behind as ash.

visual.description: SCENE_029: Hero (thinking, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Normally, deep sleep washes that adenosine away overnight.

visual.description: SCENE_030: Hero (idle_neutral, neutral) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Without sleep, adenosine locks onto your receptors and slows down neural firing.

visual.description: SCENE_031: Hero (stressed_headache, flat) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: The first physical system to fail in Randy Gardner was not his muscles.

visual.description: SCENE_032: Hero (thinking, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: It was his eyes.

visual.description: SCENE_033: Hero (pointing_target, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: On day two, Randy found that he could no longer focus his vision.

visual.description: SCENE_034: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: The tiny muscles inside his eyes were too exhausted to hold a focal length.

visual.description: SCENE_035: Hero (thinking, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: He had to stop watching television because the screen blurred into a painful glare.

visual.description: SCENE_036: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Then his friends ran a simple neurological test.

visual.description: SCENE_037: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: They asked Randy to close his eyes and identify objects strictly by touch.

visual.description: SCENE_038: Hero (thinking, flat) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: In medicine, this ability is called stereognosis.

visual.description: SCENE_039: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: It requires your parietal lobe to turn raw touch signals into a mental picture.

visual.description: SCENE_040: Hero (idea_lightbulb, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: By the end of day two, Randy's brain could no longer identify what he was holding.

visual.description: SCENE_041: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.
SCENE_042: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in office.
SCENE_043: Hero (idle_neutral, flat) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: By day three, the local newspaper had published an article about the experiment.

visual.description: SCENE_044: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: It caught the attention of Doctor William Dement from Stanford University.

visual.description: SCENE_045: Hero (idea_lightbulb, eager) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Along with Navy medical researcher John Ross, Dement rushed to observe Randy.

visual.description: SCENE_046: Hero (running_hurry, eager) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: What the doctors saw on day three was the beginning of a neurological rebellion.

visual.description: SCENE_047: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Randy's physical coordination began to crumble, a condition known as ataxia.

visual.description: SCENE_048: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: He stumbled on flat ground and struggled to repeat basic tongue twisters.

visual.description: SCENE_049: Hero (thinking, flat) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: His sense of smell became strangely hypersensitive.

visual.description: SCENE_050: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.75 in street.

scenes.narration_text: Walking past a bakery, the smell of frying donuts made him violently nauseous.

visual.description: SCENE_051: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in street.

scenes.narration_text: And then, the microsleeps began.

visual.description: SCENE_052: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_053: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: When a brain is starved of sleep for three days, it stops asking permission.

visual.description: SCENE_054: Hero (pointing_target, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: It shuts down local clusters of neurons for two to five seconds at a time.

visual.description: SCENE_055: Hero (thinking, flat) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Your eyes stay wide open. You might even still be standing upright.

visual.description: SCENE_056: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Yet slow theta waves suddenly sweep across your waking cortex.

visual.description: SCENE_057: Hero (pointing_target, flat) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: For three seconds, you are functionally blind and deaf to the outside world.

visual.description: SCENE_058: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_059: Hero (thinking, deadpan) at x=0.25 in street.

scenes.narration_text: On day four, the boundary between waking reality and dreaming dissolved.

visual.description: SCENE_060: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Dreams are supposed to stay locked inside REM sleep.

visual.description: SCENE_061: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: When you block REM sleep for four days, dreams break out into broad daylight.

visual.description: SCENE_062: Hero (shocked_fall, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: While walking down a San Diego street at night, Randy stopped in his tracks.

visual.description: SCENE_063: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in street.

scenes.narration_text: He stared in horror at a metal street sign ahead of him.

visual.description: SCENE_064: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.25 in street.

scenes.narration_text: To his exhausted visual cortex, the street sign had turned into a shadow person.

visual.description: SCENE_065: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in street.

scenes.narration_text: Hours later, he experienced his first full-blown delusion.

visual.description: SCENE_066: Hero (thinking, deadpan) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Randy became convinced that he was Paul Lowe, the famous football running back.

visual.description: SCENE_067: Hero (celebrate_win, eager) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: When his friends reminded him he was a high school student, Randy grew furious.

visual.description: SCENE_068: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in office.
SCENE_069: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: By day five, hour one hundred and twenty, hallucinations filled the room.

visual.description: SCENE_070: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Randy reported seeing the walls of his living room breathing in and out.

visual.description: SCENE_071: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: He stared at a blank plaster wall and saw a forest path opening up ahead.

visual.description: SCENE_072: Hero (pointing_target, deadpan) at x=0.75 in nature.

scenes.narration_text: Inside his brain, the thalamus—the sensory relay filter—was failing.

visual.description: SCENE_073: Hero (thinking, flat) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Random electrical static was being painted directly onto the real world.

visual.description: SCENE_074: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_075: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_076: Hero (idle_neutral, flat) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Entering day six, the science project turned into a medical endurance crisis.

visual.description: SCENE_077: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: During deep sleep, your brain activates a plumbing network called the glymphatic system.

visual.description: SCENE_078: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Fluid flushes through brain tissue, washing away toxic metabolic proteins.

visual.description: SCENE_079: Hero (idea_lightbulb, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: After six days awake, Randy's brain dishwasher had been turned off all week.

visual.description: SCENE_080: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: The neurological sludge was taking a visible toll on his body.

visual.description: SCENE_081: Hero (thinking, sad) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: His hands developed a constant fine tremor, and his face froze into a flat mask.

visual.description: SCENE_082: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.
SCENE_083: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: By day seven, his autonomic nervous system was misfiring.

visual.description: SCENE_084: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Randy felt freezing cold indoors, and his heart rate swung unpredictably.

visual.description: SCENE_085: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Emotionally, the easygoing teenager had completely vanished.

visual.description: SCENE_086: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: In his place was a defensive, irritable, and deeply paranoid patient.

visual.description: SCENE_087: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: When the prefrontal cortex goes offline, the amygdala takes the wheel unchecked.

visual.description: SCENE_088: Hero (pointing_target, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Sleep deprivation amplifies amygdala reactivity by more than sixty percent.

visual.description: SCENE_089: Hero (shocked_fall, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: To Randy on day seven, harmless questions felt like hostile interrogations.

visual.description: SCENE_090: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.
SCENE_091: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: On day eight, language itself began to fall apart.

visual.description: SCENE_092: Hero (thinking, flat) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Doctor Ross noted that Randy's speech had become slow, slurred, and monotone.

visual.description: SCENE_093: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Worse still, he could no longer hold a sentence together from start to finish.

visual.description: SCENE_094: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: He would start answering a question, get four words out, and trail into silence.

visual.description: SCENE_095: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Working memory is the mental scratchpad that holds the start of your sentence.

visual.description: SCENE_096: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: By hour one hundred and ninety-two, that scratchpad had shrunk to zero.

visual.description: SCENE_097: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_098: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_099: Hero (running_hurry, flat) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: By day nine and ten, keeping Randy awake required constant physical movement.

visual.description: SCENE_100: Hero (running_hurry, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: If he sat down for more than ten seconds, his eyes would immediately roll back.

visual.description: SCENE_101: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: So Doctor Dement and his friends kept him standing, walking, and playing games.

visual.description: SCENE_102: Hero (running_hurry, neutral) at x=0.75 in street.

scenes.narration_text: And this led to the strangest scientific paradox of the entire experiment.

visual.description: SCENE_103: Hero (idea_lightbulb, eager) at x=0.75 in void.
SCENE_104: Hero (thinking, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: During quiet paper tests, Randy functioned like someone under heavy anesthesia.

visual.description: SCENE_105: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Yet when Doctor Dement took him to play mechanical pinball, something bizarre happened.

visual.description: SCENE_106: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Randy did not just play. He beat Doctor Dement over and over again.

visual.description: SCENE_107: Hero (celebrate_win, happy) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: How could a boy who could barely speak a sentence still track a moving ball?

visual.description: SCENE_108: Hero (thinking, eager) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Quiet, repetitive thinking relies on the exhausted prefrontal cortex.

visual.description: SCENE_109: Hero (pointing_target, flat) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Fast physical games trigger primitive subcortical motor loops and adrenaline.

visual.description: SCENE_110: Hero (running_hurry, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Your survival circuits can puppet a tired body while the higher mind is dark.

visual.description: SCENE_111: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_112: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: On the morning of January eighth, nineteen sixty-four, the clock struck two hundred and sixty-four hours.

visual.description: SCENE_113: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Eleven full days without a single second of sleep.

visual.description: SCENE_114: Hero (celebrate_win, flat) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Before ending, Doctor Ross gave Randy one last exam: the Serial Sevens test.

visual.description: SCENE_115: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Start at one hundred, and subtract seven repeatedly out loud.

visual.description: SCENE_116: Hero (thinking, neutral) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Ninety-three. Eighty-six. Seventy-nine.

visual.description: SCENE_117: Hero (thinking, flat) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Seventy-two. Sixty-five. And then, Randy stopped.

visual.description: SCENE_118: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.75 in hospital.
SCENE_119: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Doctor Ross asked him why he had stopped counting.

visual.description: SCENE_120: Hero (thinking, neutral) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Randy looked at the doctor with blank eyes and said, I forgot what I was doing.

visual.description: SCENE_121: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.
SCENE_122: Hero (idle_neutral, neutral) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: After a brief press conference, Randy was taken to the Naval Hospital in San Diego.

visual.description: SCENE_123: Hero (idle_neutral, neutral) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Doctors taped electrodes to his scalp and finally let him close his eyes.

visual.description: SCENE_124: Hero (idle_neutral, happy) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: You might expect someone awake for eleven days to sleep for three days straight.

visual.description: SCENE_125: Hero (thinking, eager) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: He did not. Randy slept for exactly fourteen hours and forty minutes.

visual.description: SCENE_126: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: He woke up, ate a bowl of cereal, and told the nurses he felt fine.

visual.description: SCENE_127: Hero (celebrate_win, happy) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: But the brainwave recordings told a very different story.

visual.description: SCENE_128: Hero (thinking, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: During that sleep, Randy's brain plunged into an intense REM rebound.

visual.description: SCENE_129: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: And the real plot twist did not arrive for another forty years.

visual.description: SCENE_130: Hero (shocked_fall, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.
SCENE_131: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Let us look closer at why the human brain cannot survive without this nightly reset.

visual.description: SCENE_132: Hero (pointing_target, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Every single day, eighty-six billion neurons fire trillions of electrical signals.

visual.description: SCENE_133: Hero (idea_lightbulb, eager) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: That electrical activity produces heat, oxidative stress, and microscopic cellular debris.

visual.description: SCENE_134: Hero (thinking, neutral) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: When you fall into deep slow-wave sleep, your brain cells physically shrink by sixty percent.

visual.description: SCENE_135: Hero (shocked_fall, eager) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: That shrinkage opens wide channels between neurons so cerebrospinal fluid can rush through.

visual.description: SCENE_136: Hero (pointing_target, happy) at x=0.75 in void.
SCENE_137: Hero (idle_neutral, neutral) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Without that nightly rinse, two things happen inside your skull within forty-eight hours.

visual.description: SCENE_138: Hero (pointing_target, flat) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: First, synaptic connections become saturated and can no longer store new memories.

visual.description: SCENE_139: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Your hippocampus—the brain's inbox—literally bounces new information away.

visual.description: SCENE_140: Hero (thinking, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: Second, your emotional brakes in the medial prefrontal cortex disconnect from the amygdala.

visual.description: SCENE_141: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.75 in void.

scenes.narration_text: That is why Randy Gardner could go from laughing at a joke to shouting at his best friend in seconds.

visual.description: SCENE_142: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in office.
SCENE_143: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: And what about the body below the neck during those eleven days?

visual.description: SCENE_144: Hero (thinking, eager) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: After just four days without sleep, insulin sensitivity drops by more than thirty percent.

visual.description: SCENE_145: Hero (pointing_target, flat) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: A healthy teenager's blood sugar begins to look like someone on the verge of pre-diabetes.

visual.description: SCENE_146: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: At the same time, natural killer immune cells plummet by nearly seventy percent.

visual.description: SCENE_147: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Your blood pressure stays locked in its daytime high instead of dipping at night.

visual.description: SCENE_148: Hero (pointing_target, deadpan) at x=0.75 in hospital.
SCENE_149: Hero (idle_neutral, deadpan) at x=0.75 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: When Doctor Ross examined Randy's heart and blood vessels on day ten, he saw severe autonomic strain.

visual.description: SCENE_150: Hero (thinking, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Every time Randy inhaled, his heart rate spiked; every time he exhaled, it dropped sharply.

visual.description: SCENE_151: Hero (stressed_headache, deadpan) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: Had the experiment continued for a few more days, doctors feared his cardiovascular system could have failed.

visual.description: SCENE_152: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.25 in hospital.

scenes.narration_text: For decades, textbooks claimed extreme sleep deprivation left no permanent damage.

visual.description: SCENE_153: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.25 in classroom.

scenes.narration_text: Then, in his sixties, Randy Gardner's ability to sleep suddenly broke.

visual.description: SCENE_154: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: He was struck by severe, relentless chronic insomnia for over a decade.

visual.description: SCENE_155: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Night after night, he lay exhausted to his bones yet unable to cross into sleep.

visual.description: SCENE_156: Hero (stressed_headache, sad) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Randy himself called it karmic payback for pushing his brain past its limits at seventeen.

visual.description: SCENE_157: Hero (thinking, sad) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Modern neuroscience now knows that extreme sleep loss triggers microglial pruning.

visual.description: SCENE_158: Hero (pointing_target, deadpan) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: The brain's immune cells literally chew away healthy synaptic connections.

visual.description: SCENE_159: Hero (shocked_fall, sad) at x=0.25 in void.

scenes.narration_text: In nineteen ninety-seven, Guinness permanently shut down the sleep deprivation record.

visual.description: SCENE_160: Hero (pointing_target, neutral) at x=0.75 in office.

scenes.narration_text: Because sleep is not a luxury you can borrow against for free.

visual.description: SCENE_161: Hero (thinking, neutral) at x=0.25 in office.

scenes.narration_text: It is the nightly maintenance cycle that keeps your mind intact.

visual.description: SCENE_162: Hero (celebrate_win, happy) at x=0.25 in office.
SCENE_163: Hero (idle_neutral, happy) at x=0.25 in office.
